  MISSION STATEMENT
The City of Pasadena is dedicated to delivering exemplary municipal services, responsive to
  our entire community and consistent
  with our history, culture, and unique character.
  In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Assistive Listening Devices are available at all City
  Council Meetings. Assistive Listening headphones and neckloops can be checked out at the desk of the
  Sergeant-at-Arms, located inside the City Council Chambers. To request meeting materials in alternative
  formats or other disability-related modifications or accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting
  participation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office as soon as possible at (626) 744-4124 or
  cityclerk@cityofpasadena.net. Providing at least 72 hours advance notice will help ensure availability.

  Language translation services are available for this meeting by calling
  (626)744-4124 at least 24 hours in advance.
  Habrá servicio de interpretación disponible para éstas juntas llamando al
  (626)744-4124 por lo menos con 24 horas de anticipación.
  Meetings are broadcast live on cable Channel 3 and on the Internet at https://www.cityofpasadena.net/city-
  manager/pasadena-media/ (Click on “Watch Now”)

  Items on the agenda may not be called in order listed. Agendas and supporting documents are available
  on the Internet at http://ww2.cityofpasadena.net/councilagendas/council_agenda.asp
  Materials related to an item on this Agenda submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency to the
  Pasadena Community Development Commission after distribution of the agenda packet are available for
  public inspection in the City Clerk’s Office at 100 N. Garfield Avenue, Room S-228,
  Pasadena, during normal business hours.

   CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the month of April
  2026 as Donate Life Month in the City of Pasadena and recognized
  the many lives saved through organ donations. Alien Jolley, One
  Legacy Ambassador, accepted the proclamation, shared information
  on the importance of becoming a registered donor, and invited the
  public to participate in the Donate Life Run Walk at Azusa Pacific
  University taking place at the end of April.

  Mayor Gordo also presented a proclamation declaring April 2026 as
  Earth Month and April 22, 2026 as Earth day in the City of Pasadena.
  Lindsey Paige McCloy, Sustainability Administrator, and Lauren
  Siegel, Chair of the Environmental Advisory Commission, accepted
  the proclamation, thanked the City Council for recognizing Earth Day
  and Earth Month, shared environmentally friendly activities
  scheduled on April 18, 2026 at Villa Park and Brookside Park, and
  encouraged everyone to take action to protect the environment in
  various forms.

RECQMMENDATIQNS  CONSIDERATION OF RECONNECTING PASADENA 710 VISION
FROM OFFICERS AND  PLAN FOR THE RELINQUISHED 710 STUB PROPERTY
DEPARTMENTS  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is covered
City Manager  by the "Common Sense" exemption set forth in State CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) as CEQA only applies to projects
  that may have a significant effect on the environment; and
  (2) Review, discuss, and provide direction in the following areas:
  Immediate Next Steps:
  a. Transition the land use concepts from the Vision Plan to the
  Planning Department and initiate environmental analysis,
  entitlements, and regulatory requirements;

Council Minutes  5  03/30/2026
   b. Direct staff to continue to develop and recommend financing
  mechanisms for developing the 710 Stub area;
  c. Direct that the 710 Stub area become the City's first sustainable,
  resilient and carbon neutral district;
  d. Initiate work on options for City Council consideration of a
  governance structure to guide the development of the area;
  Restorative Justice:
  e. Acknowledge past harms to former residents, businesses and
  institutions required to vacate the relinquishment and
  surrounding area to clear the path for the freeway construction;
  f. Consider and/or further research all targets, goals, and
  programs delineated in the Restorative Justice Framework of
  the Vision Plan report as part of consideration of a Citywide
  approach to restorative justice. This includes the draft definition
  of restorative justice, targets for affordable housing, the creation
  of a community oversight committee, a community benefits
  planning framework, policies for wealth generation through
  home and business ownership, business development support,
  workforce development, and other public benefits through
  Restorative Justice;
  Land Use:
  g. Set a goal of developing a minimum of 1 ,800 residential units in
  the relinquishment area. This will include a mix of units for
  ownership and rentals of varying affordability and size;
  Mobility, Access and Reconnection:
  h. To advance reconnection, accessibility, multi-modal and active
  transportation, and community safety, include the Boulevard and
  Paseos street and access concept as the working option to carry
  forward in the land use entitlement process (item "a" above);
  Direct staff to continue to work in partnership with Caltrans
  regarding the transition of the existing freeway-to-freeway to a
  local-to-freeway/freeway-to-local access system, as well as in
  the creation of Transit Mobility Hub on Caltrans property in the
  area immediately north of and connected to the relinquishment
  area;
  Other Items:
  j. Direct staff to continue to work with Caltrans to identify a new
  location for the stormwater facility located in the southern portion
  of the relinquishment area; and
  k. Continue to grow existing partnerships - and seek new
  partnerships - with public, private, and non-profit agencies and
  entities that enhance the delivery of positive outcomes from the
  relinquishment area for the City of Pasadena and its residents
  and businesses.
  Recommendation of the Reconnecting Communities 710
  Advisory Group: At their final meeting on March 18, 2026, the
  Reconnecting Communities 710 Advisory Group voted not to take a
  position on the Vision Plan. They instead chose to submit their own
  report to the City Council "...to highlight, supplement and make

Council Minutes  6  03/30/2026
   certain recommendations regarding the Vision Plan". Please see
  Attachment C of the agenda report.

n  Brenda Han/ey-Williams, Assistant City Manager, provided
  introductory comments on the item, acknowledged the various
  departments that have collaborated on the 710 Stub project, and
  presented a clip from Amplify, the documentary commissioned by
  the City on the history of the 710 Stub. She also announced that the
  documentary won two awards, the 2025 Davey Award and the 2025
  MarCom Award. Mayor Gordo commended Suzanne Madison and
  the entire Allegra Consulting team for winning these two prestigious
  honors.

  Wendy Macias, Project Manager, provided a Powerpoint
  Presentation on the historical data of the 710-freeway site, findings
  from a UCLA study on the impacts of the 710 Freeway on Pasadena,
  oral history gathered by Allegra Consulting, historical implications,
  and redress actions. DannyParker, Chair of the 710 Advisory Group,
  thanked the City Council, City staff, the 710 Advisory Group, the
  meeting attendees, and everyone who collaborated on the 710 Stub
  project. Chair Parker provided a brief overview of the discussions
  had by the Advisory Group and subcommittees, and how they
  reached the proposed recommendations noting key themes of
  flexibility, community, and promoting the local economy, as well as
  the importance of placemaking and public art. Tina Williams, Chair
  of the Restorative Justice Standing Committee, and Wayne Brandt,
  Chair of the Land Use and Mobility Standing Committee, both
  provided recaps of topics and discussions held by their respective
  standing committees. Kate Howe, Perkins Eastman Consulting,
  provided a Powerpoint presentation summarizing the proposed 710
  Vision Plan. She presented information on the concepts of the plan,
  including flexible land use, restorative justice elements, physical
  reconnection of the land, and transportation frameworks/goals for
  the project. Vaughan Davies, Perkins Eastman Consulting,
  presented the design principles and vision concepts for the street
  design framework and urban spaces. David Grannis, reported on the
  numerous regional partnerships involved in the ongoing project
  (Caltrans, SCAG, Metro, etc.). Jennifer Paige, Planning Director,
  reported on the next steps to develop a Specific Plan for the area.

  Councilmembers Jones and Cole advocated for careful
  considerations regarding where traffic is redistributed in the project
  area to minimize impacts to surrounding areas.

  Blair Milter, Pasadena resident, urged the City Council to take
  the 710 Advisory Group's recommendations into careful
  consideration and utilize suitable metrics to measure and define
  success.

  Council Minutes  7  03/30/2026
   Veronica Dolleschel, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City
  to consider elements of housing, traffic patterns, and repairing
  the harms of the past as the 710 Stub project moves forward.
n  The following individuals expressed support for the proposed
  restorative justice initiatives as a means of accountability for past
  harms and/or provided related comments:

  Bert Newton, Pasadena resident
  Jacqueline Kuykenball, Greenline Housing
  Pastor Kerwin Manning, Pasadena resident

  Wes Hampton, Pasadena Voices Orange Grove Residents
  Council, requested access to the traffic simulation study for the
  proposed project, and advocated for speed traffic cameras and
  implementing noise reduction technology.

  Gabo Lizardo, Chair of Arts & Culture Commission, advocated
  for the City to prioritize public art and cultural infrastructure as
  part of the proposed project.

  Thomas Tai, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
  to prioritize increased housing objectives in the proposed
  project.

  Michael Warner II, Pasadena resident, emphasized the
  importance of maintaining emergency access points to
  Huntington Hospital when implementing the 710 Stub Vision
  Plan.

  Catherine Jurca, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  regarding the project and study area boundaries, and
  requested a more definitive study report.

  Marcus Renner, Pasadena resident, advocated for larger public
  spaces, the creation of an interpretive center to presen/e
  community history, and a community-driven planning process.

  Michael Canavan, Pasadena resident, encouraged more
  ambitious housing goals as being essential to reconnecting
  communities and addressing past displacement.

  Ed Riddle, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding
  affordability of senior housing and its lack of emphasis in the
  proposed project.

  Councilmember Madison thanked the 710 Advisory Group, City staff,
  and all stakeholders for their collaborative efforts on the project. He
  requested City staff to return in two weeks with a decision-making
  framework and recommended sequencing of such decisions.

  Council Minutes  8  03/30/2026
   Mayor Gordo also requested information on feasibility and financing
  for the entire project, various ownership models, governance models
  for long-term management, and potential impacts of SB79
  implementation and increased density in the design and
  implementation of the 710 Vision Plan.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, by consensus of the
  City Council, the information was received and filed, with the item to
  return on April 13,2026.
